text: ← Advanced contents AVAILABLE CHAPTERS WHAT YOU WILL LEARNDerive corotation charge density, compare SI and Gaussian units, and distinguish light-cylinder limits, net charge and pair plasma. Connect to foundations: The classical electron radius and Thomson scattering ↗ Compare solution assumptions and boundary data in the solution library ↗ 01Rotation creates a corotation electric field A highly conducting corotating plasma satisfies E+v×B = 0 locally. Insert v = Ω×r and first examine a flat-spacetime, quasistatic approximation to the required charge density. E=−(Ω×r)×B, ∇·E=ρeε₀ (SI) ρe denotes charge density, not mass density. Corotation can require a net charge; this alone does not determine the total electron–positron population. 02Apply a vector identity to obtain GJ density ∇·(v×B)=B·(∇×v)−v·(∇×B), ∇×(Ω×r)=2Ω ρe=ε₀[−2Ω·B+v·(∇×B)] Neglecting the current-related curl-B term in the near zone gives the Goldreich–Julian density scale. Keeping the omitted term visible clarifies where the approximation fails. ρGJ≈−2ε₀Ω·B (SI) ρGJ≈−Ω·B2πc (Gauss) nGJ≡|ρGJ|e Gaussian corotation includes 1/c and Gauss’s law reads ∇·E = 4πρe. Inserting a magnetic field measured in gauss directly into the SI formula is incorrect. 03Estimate the scale from period and field Ω=2πP, nGJ≈6.94×1010B∥ / 1012 GP / s cm−3 (magnitude) B∥ is the magnitude of the local component parallel to Ω. An aligned dipole with polar field Bp has surface Bz = Bp(3cos²θ−1)/2. The approximate charge changes sign near θ = 54.7°. The panel estimates the near field at the surface of a 12 km star using an aligned dipole. It does not solve field back-reaction, relativistic frame dragging or the global magnetospheric current. 04The light cylinder and a polar-cap estimate Rigid corotation has speed Ωr⊥ at cylindrical radius r⊥ and cannot extend beyond the light cylinder. The dipole line r = req sin²θ gives a geometric estimate of the open polar cap. RLC=cΩ≈4.77×10⁴(Ps) km sin²θpc≈R*RLC, rpc≈R*√(R*RLC) This cap estimate assumes an aligned dipole whose last closed line reaches the light cylinder. Real fields open and carry currents; a vacuum dipole is not an exact exterior solution. 05Connect net charge to acceleration and radiation A dense pair plasma can supply the required net charge through n₊−n₋ while n₊+n₋ greatly exceeds nGJ. The GJ number scale is not automatically the total density to use in scattering rates. Insufficient charge can leave an unscreened field along B and permit particle acceleration, radiation and pair creation. A density scale alone does not determine gap locations or the emitted spectrum. These diagrams recompute the corotation approximation, not global paper magnetospheres or observed pulses. Use them to inspect local validity and charge sign. CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING Pause and work it out. At fixed field and location, double the spin period. How do GJ charge magnitude, light-cylinder radius and aligned-dipole polar-cap radius change? Show the answer and reasoning Charge magnitude halves, light-cylinder radius doubles, and the aligned-dipole cap radius decreases by √2. The last result is a geometric estimate, not a solution for the global magnetosphere. REFERENCES & PHYSICAL INPUTS Explanations and derivations are written for this guide. References may use different notation or normalization. Panel methods and approximations are stated in the text.
